title: Power Automate: view property values inline on cards in the new cloud flow designer
summary: The briefing's behaviour, maker controls and licensing statements are supported by the roadmap and Microsoft Learn. A minor clarification should acknowledge an older release-plan entry that gives a different default and target date; the current roadmap explicitly retains the side pane as the default.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The feature displays property values from multiple steps inline on action cards at design time.
claims.quote: When you add an action, you can view property values for multiple steps at design time, or output values for multiple steps at runtime. The inline view shows this information directly on the cards

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The inline view displays output values from multiple steps on cards at runtime.
claims.quote: you can view property values for multiple steps at design time, or output values for multiple steps at runtime. The inline view shows this information directly on the cards

claims.claim: Inline display lets makers review and compare values across several steps at once.
claims.quote: The inline view shows this information directly on the cards, so you can review and compare values across several steps at once.

claims.claim: Without inline view, selecting individual cards shows one step's value at a time in the side pane.
claims.quote: Without the inline view, you select each card individually to see its value in the side pane, and you can view only one step's value at a time.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationales
claims.claim: The side pane remains the default and the inline view is a maker choice, represented as user-opt-in.
claims.quote: You can choose which experience you prefer. The current side pane experience remains the default. You can switch to the inline view whenever you want and switch back at any time.
claims.fix: Keep user-opt-in and the current roadmap default. Add to What's changing: "An older release-plan entry indexed by Microsoft Learn describes inline display as the default and gives February 2026 as its general-availability target; this briefing follows the current roadmap record's side-pane default and June CY2026 target." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/release-plan/2025wave2/power-automate/view-property-value-expanded-inline-new-cloud-designer. The indexed excerpt says "The feature shows all that information inline by default" and "Feb 2026"; opening that URL now leads to the archived release-wave overview.
